explanations.Explain which accepted and rejected wire: Satisfied. TestValidateMicroUSDEnforcesWireMonetaryContract in daemon/internal/protocol/goal_boundary_validator_test.go directly calls production ValidateMicroUSD and checks whether its returned error agrees with each expected outcome. Accepted strings are "0", "1", "1000000", "9007199254740992" (above the JSON-safe-integer maximum), and "9223372036854775807" (MaxInt64). Rejected strings cover empty input; leading zeroes ("00", "01"); signs ("-1", "-0", "+1"); fractional, exponential and hexadecimal notation ("1.5", "1e6", "0x10"); leading, trailing and embedded whitespace (" 1", "1 ", "1\n", "1\t0"); non-ASCII digits (U+0661); "NaN"; two 19-digit overflows ("9223372036854775808", "9999999999999999999"); and the 20-digit "10000000000000000000". The 19-digit overflow cases distinguish numeric range enforcement from a mere length restriction. Evidence: production goal_validation.go documents PostgreSQL signed-bigint storage and enforces the bound with strconv.ParseUint(value, 10, 63); docs/design/contracts.md specifies decimal-string microusd on wire and bigint storage; contracts/v1/common.schema.json#/definitions/Microusd encodes the same upper bound. Thus an otherwise correctly formatted decimal exceeding MaxInt64 is not transportable under the shared contract. Conversely, monetary strings are not restricted to the JSON-number safe-integer range. I inspected coordinator attempt-0001 rather than rerunning its gates: both frozen commands have exit_code 0, and the raw Go event stream records this named test running and passing once, with all 23 subtests passing and no skips or failures.
explanations.Explain why each rejected commit path is: Satisfied. TestValidateCommitPathRejectsUnnormalizedPaths directly calls production validateCommitPath and requires a non-nil error for every case. The empty string violates the minimum length of one character; 1025 repeated ASCII characters exceed the 1024-rune maximum; "dir/\xff" violates valid UTF-8; "/etc/passwd" violates the prohibition on a leading slash and absolute paths; "dir/fi\x00le" contains forbidden NUL; "dir\\file", "C:\\dir\\file", and "\\\\server\\share\\file" contain forbidden backslashes, covering backslash separators, Windows-absolute syntax and UNC syntax respectively; "dir//file" contains a forbidden repeated slash; and "..", "../file", "dir/../file", and "dir/.." contain forbidden complete parent-directory segments in sole, leading, embedded and trailing positions. Even "dir/../file" is rejected rather than resolved to another path. These expectations match goal_validation.go and contracts/v1/common.schema.json#/definitions/CommitPath; docs/design/contracts.md requires artifact paths to bind exact Git tree paths without host-filesystem normalization. The raw coordinator event stream records this named test running and passing once, with all 13 subtests passing and no skips or failures; the stored validator output and test-binary listing corroborate both required test names. Scope verification found only the permitted new test file, with production code, existing tests and gate configuration unchanged. A read-only invocation of the evaluator's require_current_subject recomputed the current source identity and changed-path set, matching the sealed subject and manifest exactly.
